mainTopic: The 'hanging by a hair' law of מעילה, and laws that only have support in the תורה
overview: The גמרא first finishes searching for the law of מעילה that the משנה calls 'like mountains hanging by a hair'. The stone-or-beam case makes sense once we see it is about a גזבר. The house case also makes sense according to רב, so neither of these is the 'hanging' law. The answer is רבא's case: the messenger is guilty even though he had no reason to suspect the money was הקדש. Next, a ברייתא and רב פפא explain that נגעים has many פסוקים and few הלכות, while אהלות has few פסוקים and many הלכות. Then the גמרא goes through the משנה's list of laws that 'have something to rely on': דינין, עבודות, טהרות and טומאות. Each time it asks, 'They are written in the תורה!' Each time it answers that the משנה means one detail that is only hinted at: רבי's money reading of נפש תחת נפש, הולכת הדם, the forty סאה of a מקוה, and the lentil-size of a שרץ. The same question is then asked about עריות, and its answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The stone case is about a Temple treasurer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the stone-or-beam case as talking about a גזבר, so the case is logical and is not the 'hanging' law.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are dealing with a Temple treasurer who was given charge of the building stones. Wherever he puts a stone, it is resting in his own area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes pushing back on the idea that the stone-or-beam case is the 'hanging by a hair' law. It shows the case makes good sense: the man who picks up the stone is the גזבר, the one put in charge of the stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזבר may move the stones around, because wherever they lie they are still under his care. So lifting a stone is not מעילה. Handing it to someone else is, since he had no permission to do that. Since the law now makes good sense, it is not the 'mountains hanging by a hair' law.

keyTerms.meaning: Treasurer of the בית המקדש, in charge of its property
Misusing הקדש property for personal benefit

phrases.english: With a treasurer to whom were entrusted
the building stones, we are dealing,
for anywhere that it is resting,
it is resting in his own domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּגִזְבָּר הַמְּסוּרוֹת לוֹ אַבְנֵי בִנְיָן עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection, begun just before this amud, of the suggestion that the stone-or-beam case is the 'hanging' law.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the stone-or-beam case is the 'hanging by a hair' law.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case is not strange once we see it is about a גזבר who is allowed to handle the stones.

steps.title: New suggestion: the case of building the stone into a house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the later part of the משנה, about building the stone into one's house, is the 'hanging' law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, take the later clause: if he built the stone into his house, he has not done מעילה until he lives under it for a פרוטה's worth. But once he has changed the stone, why should it matter whether he lives there? This must be the law 'like mountains hanging by a hair'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new candidate for the 'hanging' law: the case of building a הקדש stone into one's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building the stone into a wall changes it, and changing an item normally counts as using it. So it seems strange that he is only guilty once he lives under it a פרוטה's worth. Because this rule seems to have no clear reason, it looks like the 'hanging' law.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount for מעילה
Like mountains hanging by a hair: many laws with very little source

phrases.english: Rather, from the latter clause:
if he built it into his house,
he has not committed מעילה
until he lives under it a פרוטה's worth.
Since he has changed it,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי דָּר וּמָה לִי לָא דָּר,
phrases.english: what difference is it whether he lives there or does not live there?
This is the law 'like mountains hanging by a hair'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the stone case was explained away, the גמרא moves to the next clause of the same משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'hanging' law is the rule that building the stone into a house is only מעילה once he lives there a פרוטה's worth.

steps.title: רב explains the house case, so it is not strange
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion, because רב explains that the stone was only laid over an opening and was never changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty? Perhaps the case is as רב explained, for רב said: he placed the stone over the opening of a skylight. If he lives in the house, yes, it is מעילה. If he does not live there, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the house case is not strange at all if we read it the way רב does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, the stone was only laid over an opening and was not built into the wall, so it was never changed. He gains nothing from it unless he actually lives there. That makes living there the logical point of מעילה, so this is not the 'hanging' law either.

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps it is as Rav explained.
For Rav said:
For example, where he placed it over the opening of a skylight.
If he lives in it, yes;
if he does not live in it, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the house case as the 'hanging' law.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed the stone was changed. רב says it was only placed over an opening, so living there is the real benefit.

steps.title: Back to רבא: the messenger had no reason to check
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes the 'hanging' law is רבא's case after all, and explains why it differs from spending known הקדש money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it really is as רבא said. And as for what bothered you, that it is just like someone who spends הקדש money on everyday things: there, he knew he had הקדש coins, so he should have checked. Here, did the messenger know? That is why it is like mountains hanging by a hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבא's explanation and answers the earlier challenge against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רבא's case seemed ordinary, like anyone who mistakenly spends הקדש money. The difference is that such a person knew he owned הקדש coins and was careless not to check. The messenger had no idea, yet he is still guilty, and that surprising rule is the 'hanging by a hair' law.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (returning to an earlier view)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'mountains hanging by a hair' law of מעילה is רבא's case: the messenger is guilty even though he had no reason to suspect the money was הקדש.

phrases.english: Rather, actually it is as Rava said.
phrases.notes: רבא's case came up before: the owner remembered the money was הקדש, but the messenger who spent it never knew.

phrases.english: And as for what was difficult for you:

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַמּוֹצִיא מְעוֹת הֶקְדֵּשׁ לְחוּלִּין,
phrases.english: that it is just like one who spends הקדש money for ordinary use,
there, he certainly knows
that there are coins of הקדש,
so he should have checked.
Here, did he know?!
This is the law like mountains hanging by a hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the house case is rejected, the גמרא returns to רבא's earlier explanation and defends it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's case is the 'hanging' law. A messenger who had no reason to suspect the money was הקדש is still guilty of מעילה, unlike someone who knowingly kept הקדש coins and should have checked.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה and a ברייתא on נגעים and אהלות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'little Scripture, many הלכות' and brings a ברייתא that applies it to נגעים and אהלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: little Scripture and many הלכות. A ברייתא taught: נגעים and אהלות have little Scripture and many הלכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a phrase from the משנה and brings a ברייתא that names which topics it is talking about. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה described some laws as 'mountains hanging by a hair': few פסוקים but many details. The ברייתא names two such topics, נגעים and אהלות.

keyTerms.meaning: Few פסוקים, little written in the תורה
The laws of צרעת, skin afflictions
טומאה spread by being under one roof with a dead body
A Sage taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Little Scripture and many halakhot.
A Sage taught: leprosy and tents,
have little Scripture and many halakhot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion of the משנה's phrase 'little Scripture, many הלכות.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נגעים and אהלות are listed as having few פסוקים and many הלכות.

steps.title: But נגעים Has Many פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא, because נגעים has a lot written about it in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does נגעים have little Scripture? נגעים has a lot of Scripture!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's claim that נגעים has few פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה spends two long chapters on צרעת. So calling נגעים a topic with 'little Scripture' seems plainly wrong.

phrases.english: Leprosy has little Scripture?
Leprosy has a great deal of Scripture!

steps.triggerLanguage: נְגָעִים מִקְרָא מוּעָט? נְגָעִים מִקְרָא מְרוּבֶּה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that נגעים has few פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה plainly has many פסוקים about נגעים, so the claim contradicts the text of the תורה.

steps.title: רב פפא: נגעים and אהלות Are Opposites
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rereads the ברייתא: נגעים has many פסוקים and few הלכות, and אהלות has few פסוקים and many הלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said, this is what it means: נגעים has much Scripture and few הלכות; אהלות has little Scripture and many הלכות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by explaining that the ברייתא is contrasting the two topics, not grouping them together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only אהלות fits 'little Scripture, many הלכות.' נגעים was mentioned as its opposite. This removes the problem from step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means, a rereading of the text

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said, this is what it is saying:
Leprosy has much Scripture and few halakhot,
tents have little Scripture and many halakhot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא as a contrast between two topics
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא puts both נגעים and אהלות in the same category.
steps.terutzMaskana: נגעים is the opposite case: many פסוקים, few הלכות. Only אהלות has few פסוקים and many הלכות.

steps.title: What Difference Does It Make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference it makes whether a topic has many or few פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this information matters. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know which topic has more פסוקים, the גמרא wants to know what we should do with that fact.

phrases.english: And what is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the practical use of רב פפא's distinction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the number of פסוקים compared to הלכות affects how one learns.

steps.title: Where to Look When You Are Unsure
steps.stepSummary: If you are unsure about נגעים, look in the פסוקים. If you are unsure about אהלות, look in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you have a doubt about נגעים, study the פסוקים. If you have a doubt about אהלות, study the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference tells you where to go to find the answer to a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נגעים is spelled out in the תורה, so the פסוקים are the main place to look. אהלות is mostly תורה שבעל פה, so the answers are in the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: נגעים: many פסוקים, few הלכות, so check the פסוקים. אהלות: few פסוקים, many הלכות, so check the משנה.

phrases.english: If you have a doubt about a matter in leprosy,
look into the verses,
and if you have a doubt about a matter in tents,
look into the Mishnah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The distinction tells you where to look for answers: the פסוקים for נגעים, the משנה for אהלות.

steps.title: Money Laws Are Written Explicitly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the word דינין from the משנה and asks why it is described as only having support, when money laws are written in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says דינין. But they are written explicitly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed דינין among things that 'have something to rely on,' as if they were only hinted at. But the תורה writes out many money laws, so the description seems wrong.

phrases.english: Monetary laws.
They are written explicitly!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's description of דינין as only 'having something to rely on.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Money laws are written outright in the תורה, so they are more than merely supported.

steps.title: It Follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's wording is needed only for the view of רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for the view of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers briefly. The next steps quote the ברייתא of רבי to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not talking about money laws that are written outright. It means cases like רבי's, where a money payment is learned through a hint and not stated directly.

phrases.english: It is needed only for the view of Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means all money laws.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a law like רבי's, which is learned indirectly from the פסוקים.

steps.title: רבי: A Life for a Life Means Money
steps.stepSummary: רבי teaches that 'נפש תחת נפש' means a payment of money.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי says, 'a life for a life' means money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא of רבי that it referred to in step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק sounds like it demands an actual life. רבי reads it as a money payment, which is exactly the kind of law that 'has something to rely on.'

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi says:
"Life for life" means money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source behind step 11's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'נפש תחת נפש' refers to a money payment.

steps.title: Maybe It Means an Actual Life
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the פסוק might mean an actual life instead of money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say money, or perhaps it means an actual life?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי raises the obvious other reading of the פסוק. This sets up his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'נפש תחת נפש' sound like they mean a real life, so רבי needs to show why money is the correct reading.

phrases.english: Do you say money,
or is it only an actual life?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר מָמוֹן, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא נֶפֶשׁ מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי's reading from step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'נפש תחת נפש' means money or an actual life.

steps.title: The Word Giving Links the Two Verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי proves it means money: the word 'giving' appears in both פסוקים, and in the earlier פסוק it means money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'giving' is said below, and 'giving' is said above. Just as there it means money, so here it means money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי proves his reading by linking two פסוקים that use the same word, which is a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier פסוק (ונתן בפלילים) clearly talks about paying money. The later פסוק (ונתתה נפש תחת נפש) uses the same word 'give,' so it also means money. Since the law is learned through a link and is not written outright, it is the kind the משנה calls 'having something to rely on.'

keyTerms.meaning: The later פסוק / the earlier פסוק
Just as there, so too here

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, 'נפש תחת נפש' means money, learned through the shared word 'giving.' This is why the משנה says דינין 'have something to rely on.'

phrases.english: Giving is stated below,
phrases.notes: 'Below' is the later פסוק, 'you shall give life for life' (שמות 21:23).

phrases.english: and giving is stated above.
phrases.notes: 'Above' is the earlier פסוק, 'he shall give as the judges decide' (שמות 21:22).

phrases.english: Just as there it is money,
so too here it is money.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֶמְרָה נְתִינָה לְמַטָּה. וְנֶאֶמְרָה נְתִינָה לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 with a proof.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה built on the word 'giving' in שמות 21:22 and 21:23.

steps.title: עבודות are written in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes עבודות from the משנה and asks why it is described as only having support, when the laws of עבודות are written in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentioned 'sacrificial services.' But they are written openly in the תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, עבודות. It asks the same kind of question it asked about דינין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה put עבודות in a group that only 'has support' in the תורה. But the תורה clearly writes out the steps of the קרבנות. So that label seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The services done with קרבנות in the בית המקדש
They are clearly written (in the תורה)

phrases.english: Sacrificial services.
They are clearly written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same pattern of question as step 10, now applied to the next item in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's description of עבודות as only 'having support'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The laws of עבודות are written openly in the תורה, so calling them only 'supported' does not fit.

steps.title: It refers to carrying the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's wording is needed only for הולכת הדם, carrying the blood to the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was only needed for carrying the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about one specific step: carrying the blood to the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most עבודות are written openly in the תורה. But the rules for הולכה are not written directly. They only come from a hint, so for הולכה the label 'has support' fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying the blood of a קרבן to the מזבח

phrases.english: It was only needed
for carrying the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 by narrowing the משנה to one specific step of the service.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to describe all עבודות as only 'supported'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means only הולכת הדם, whose rules come from a hint.

steps.title: The תורה calls collecting the blood by the word for carrying
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that 'והקריבו' means collecting the blood. The תורה used a word that elsewhere means carrying, as in the פסוק about carrying the limbs to the ramp.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And they shall offer' means collecting the blood. The תורה said it with a word that means carrying. As it says: 'And the כהן shall offer the whole and burn it on the מזבח.' And the Master said: this means carrying the limbs to the ramp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where the hint about הולכה comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses 'והקריבו' to describe קבלת הדם. In another פסוק, the same word 'והקריב' clearly means carrying the limbs to the כבש, since burning them is mentioned separately. So the תורה described collecting with a carrying word. That links the two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Collecting the blood of the קרבן in a vessel
The ramp leading up to the מזבח

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'And they shall offer,'
this is collecting the blood.
And the Merciful One expressed it in the language of carrying,
as it is written: 'And the priest shall offer the whole
and burn it on the altar,'
and the Master said:
this is carrying the limbs to the ramp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows where the hint for the rules of הולכה comes from.
steps.raayaObject: That הולכה is tied to קבלה through the wording of the תורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on ויקרא א:ה, together with ויקרא א:יג

steps.title: Carrying follows the rules of collecting
steps.stepSummary: The conclusion is that הולכה is not taken out of the category of קבלה. The same rules apply to both.
steps.simpleTranslation: This means that carrying should not be taken out of the category of collecting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states what we learn from the shared wording: הולכה has the same rules as קבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the תורה described קבלה with a word for carrying, the two are treated as one category. The rules for collecting the blood apply to carrying it too. This comes only from a hint, which is why the משנה said עבודות 'have support'.

keyTerms.meaning: That is to say / this teaches

steps.whatToRemember: The rules for הולכת הדם are learned from קבלת הדם only through a hint in the wording. That is why the משנה calls עבודות 'supported'.

phrases.english: That is to say that carrying
should not be taken out of the category of collecting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical lesson from the proof in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הולכה follows the same rules as קבלה, learned only by a hint.

steps.title: Purity laws are written in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes טהרות from the משנה and asks why it is described as only having support, when the laws of purity are written in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentioned 'purity laws.' But they are written openly in the תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, טהרות. It asks the same question again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה writes a great deal about טומאה and טהרה. So it seems strange to say these laws only 'have support'.

phrases.english: Purity laws.
They are clearly written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same pattern of question for the next item in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's description of טהרות as only 'having support'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Purity laws are written openly in the תורה.

steps.title: It refers to the size of a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's wording is needed only for the size of a מקוה, which is not written in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was only needed for the size of a מקוה, which is not written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about how big a מקוה must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה clearly requires immersing in water. But it never gives the minimum amount of water. That detail only has 'support', which is why the label fits.

keyTerms.meaning: The minimum size of a מקוה

phrases.english: It was only needed
for the measure of a ritual bath, which is not written,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by narrowing the משנה to the size of a מקוה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to describe all purity laws as only 'supported'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means only the size of a מקוה, which is not written.

steps.title: The verses hint at a body-sized amount of water
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוקים that one must immerse in a מקוה whose water covers the whole body. That is one אמה by one אמה, three אמות high.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'He shall wash his flesh in water' means in the water of a מקוה. 'All his flesh' means water that his whole body can go into. How much is that? One אמה by one אמה, three אמות high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show the hint in the פסוקים for the size of a מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In water' teaches that one must use a מקוה. 'All his flesh' teaches that the water must cover the whole body at once. The ברייתא turns that into a measurement: 1×1×3 אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, roughly the length of a forearm

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'And he shall wash his flesh in water'
in the water of a ritual bath.
'All his flesh'
means water in which his whole body can go in,
And how much is that?

phrases.aramaic: אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה בְּרוּם שָׁלֹשׁ אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: One cubit by one cubit, three cubits high.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows where the hint for the size of a מקוה comes from.
steps.raayaObject: That a מקוה must be big enough to cover the whole body
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on the פסוקים of washing in ויקרא

steps.title: חכמים set the מקוה at forty סאה
steps.stepSummary: חכמים calculated that this amount of water equals forty סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים calculated that the water of a מקוה is forty סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by turning the size into the well-known amount: forty סאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 1×1×3 אמות measurement is converted by חכמים into a volume of forty סאה. The תורה only hints at a body-sized amount. The exact number comes from חכמים, so this is a clear case of 'having support'.
steps.whatToRemember: A kosher מקוה needs forty סאה. The תורה only hints at it ('all his flesh'), and חכמים worked out the exact amount.

phrases.english: And the Sages estimated
the water of a ritual bath at forty se'ah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by giving the final amount of water.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מקוה must hold forty סאה, a size only hinted at in the תורה.

steps.title: The laws of טומאה are written in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'טומאות' from the משנה and asks why it needs support when the laws of impurity are written in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentioned טומאות. But they are clearly written in the תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה's list, טומאות. It asks the same question it asked about טהרות: these laws are already written in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said some laws only 'have something to support them', meaning they are not fully written. But the תורה spends whole chapters on impurity. So why put טומאות in this group?

keyTerms.meaning: They are clearly written (in the תורה)

phrases.english: Impurities.
They are clearly written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question pattern as step 19, now asked about טומאות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה listing טומאות among laws that only have support.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Laws written clearly in the תורה do not need mere 'support'.

steps.title: The משנה means the lentil-size measure of a creeping animal
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה means the size of a כעדשה from a שרץ, which is not written in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for the lentil-size of a שרץ, which is not written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is not talking about impurity in general. It means one detail: how much of a שרץ makes a person impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic law that a dead שרץ makes things impure is written. But the amount, the size of a lentil, is not written. That detail is the part that only 'has support'.

keyTerms.meaning: A creeping animal that makes things impure when dead

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying טומאות are unwritten. Only the exact measure is unwritten.

phrases.english: It is needed only
for a lentil-size from a creeping animal,
which is not written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the משנה to one unwritten detail
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means all the laws of impurity.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means only the lentil-size measure of a שרץ.

steps.title: A ברייתא reads 'of them' and 'them' about the creeping animal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows two words in the פסוקים that seem to point in opposite directions: 'בהם' and 'מהם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'בהם' (them). You might think only the whole animal; so the פסוק says 'מהם' (of them). You might think any part of it; so the פסוק says 'בהם'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where the lentil-size measure comes from. The ברייתא sets up two words that seem to pull against each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מהם' (of them) means even a piece is enough, so you don't need the whole animal. 'בהם' (them) sounds like the whole animal, so not just any tiny piece. The ברייתא now has to explain how both can be true.

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'them' —
you might think only all of them (the whole animal),
so the verse says: 'of them'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:32. 'Of them' means a part is enough.

phrases.english: You might think even any part of them,
so the verse says: 'them'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the lentil-size answer of step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That the measure of a שרץ is learned from the פסוקים only as a hint.

steps.title: A part that is like the whole
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא settles the two words: you need a piece that is like the whole animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? Not until he touches a part of it that is like the whole of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how both words fit together. It answers that the piece must be big enough to count like a whole animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מהם' teaches that a part is enough. 'בהם' teaches that it must be a meaningful part, one that is 'like the whole'. So both words are kept.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (how do these fit together)
A part of it that is like the whole

phrases.english: How so?
Not until he touches a part of it
that is like the whole of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the two words raised in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combining two words into one rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either only a whole animal, or any tiny piece.
steps.terutzMaskana: A part that is like the whole.

steps.title: חכמים set it at the size of a lentil
steps.stepSummary: חכמים measured 'a part like the whole' as a lentil's size, because the חומט starts out that small.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים measured it as a lentil's size, because the חומט at its beginning is the size of a lentil.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the exact amount: the size of a lentil. It explains this with the smallest creeping animal, the חומט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A newborn חומט is only the size of a lentil, and it is a whole animal. So a lentil-sized piece of any שרץ counts 'like the whole'. This is the unwritten measure the משנה meant.

keyTerms.meaning: A small creeping animal (the smallest of the שרצים)

steps.whatToRemember: The lentil-size of a שרץ is not written in the תורה. חכמים measured it, using the hint of 'בהם' and 'מהם'. That is why the משנה says טומאות only 'have support'.

phrases.english: The Sages measured it as a lentil's size,
because the ḥomet —
at its beginning is a lentil's size.
phrases.notes: He means when it is first born, it is that small.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the exact size for the rule in step 26.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The measure for impurity from a שרץ is a lentil's size.

steps.title: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה: a lizard's tail
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה gives a different picture for the measure: like a lizard's tail.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: like a lizard's tail.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא gives his own way to describe the measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of the newborn חומט, he uses a lizard's tail as the example of 'a part that is like the whole'. It is a second opinion inside the same ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
Like a lizard's tail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another opinion on the measure in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The measure is like a lizard's tail.

steps.title: עריות are written in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'עריות' from the משנה and asks the same question: they are written in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentioned עריות. But they are clearly written in the תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next item in the משנה's list, עריות, and asks the same question again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden relationships are listed openly in the תורה. So why does the משנה say they only 'have support'?

phrases.english: Forbidden relations.
They are clearly written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question pattern as step 23, now about עריות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה listing עריות among laws that only have support.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The forbidden relations are written clearly in the תורה.

steps.title: The answer about forbidden relations begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: 'it is needed only…', and the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer with the same pattern as before. The rest of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like with טהרות and טומאות, the גמרא will point to one detail of עריות that is not written. Here only the opening words appear.

phrases.english: It is needed only

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the משנה to one unwritten detail (answer continues)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means all the laws of עריות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means only one unwritten detail (explained next).
